title.narrative: Shelter and WASH response Chikwawa flooding cyclon Idai, Malawi

description.narrative: 15.608 people / 4.011 households (note that the average household size is smaller than usually due to families splitting up during the floods and staying in different camps) with 2.295 people/459 households benefiting of shelter and 13.313 people/ 3.552 households being provided with WASH. The WASH component is aimed at Internally Displaces Persons (IDPs) from the Chikwawa district who have been accommodated in a total of 40 camps, of whom the project will support 14. These are people from the Chikwawa district whose villages were destroyed by the floods in March. The people have found refuge either in churches or schools; others have been assigned a place by the Department of Disaster Management Affairs (DoDMA) district administrators or partly also by private people where they have built their temporary dwellings, which mostly consist of tarpaulins and a grass roof. The camp population consists of all social classes, elders, village leaders, women, men, children, people with disabilities and chronic diseases.459 households in Camp Mwalija, which is already supported with food supply, Non-Food Items (NFIs) and WASH activities as part of the German embassy project, will receive additional Shelter Kits as part of this project.

Project Outcome:Targeted cyclone affected communities in Chikwawa (Malawi) and Chimanimani (Zimbabwe) district have restored their access to shelter, safe drinking water, safely managed and dignified sanitation facilities and adopt safe hygiene practices to mitigate public health risks.
Shelter and WASH response in Chikwawa, Malawi after Cyclone Idai
